..summary: The same five-member card-type union is declared four times, costing five casts to convert between identical types

evidence: `LibraryCardType`, `CardShape` (src/lib/cardShape.ts:13), `CardType` (src/lib/bridge/protocol.ts) and `DetectedType` (src/components/ImportPNG.tsx:10) all spell out `"character" | "lorebook" | "script" | "scenario" | "persona"`; only DetectedType differs, by adding `| null`.

src/lib/bridge/client.ts writes `c.cardType as CardType` at lines 281, 312, 360, 367 and 374 solely to cross between LibraryCardType and CardType — an assertion that can never fail and communicates nothing.

protocol.ts documents that it must stay dependency-free, so its own `CardType` is defensible; `CardShape` and `DetectedType` have no such justification and sit in the same src/ tree as `LibraryCardType`.
detail.suggestion: Keep `LibraryCardType` in src/types/index.ts as the single app-side name. Have src/lib/cardShape.ts export `type CardShape = LibraryCardType` (or drop the alias and use LibraryCardType directly), replace ImportPNG's `DetectedType` with `LibraryCardType | null`, and in src/lib/bridge/client.ts add one line asserting protocol compatibility (`const _check: CardType = null as unknown as LibraryCardType`) so the five per-call-site `as CardType` casts can be deleted.

..summary: LibraryCard fakes a tagged union, forcing 17 unchecked casts to recover the type it already knows

evidence: src/types/index.ts declares `LibraryCard` with `cardType: LibraryCardType`, `cardData?: TavernCardV2` and `rawData?: unknown`, with comments explaining which slot is populated for which cardType — the invariant is documented in prose rather than in the type.

Because the shape is not discriminated, `switch (card.cardType)` cannot narrow `rawData`, so consumers assert: App.tsx:229-238 (`card.rawData as LoreBook` / `as ScriptCard` / `as ScenarioCard` / `as PersonaCard`), Library.tsx:132-138 (the same four), ImportPNG.tsx:132/141/150/159 and DecodePNG.tsx:116-119 (`parsed as LoreBook` etc.), and bridge/client.ts:292 (`c.rawData as Record<string, string>`).
Nothing validates the payload before the cast, so a lorebook record whose rawData is malformed reaches LoreBookEditor typed as a valid LoreBook.
detail.suggestion: Replace the flat interface in src/types/index.ts with a discriminated union over `cardType`: a shared `LibraryCardBase` holding id/name/pngData/imageSrc/platform/tags/createdAt/updatedAt, then `{ cardType: "character"; cardData: TavernCardV2 }` and `{ cardType: "lorebook"; rawData: LoreBook }` / `"script"; rawData: ScriptCard` / `"scenario"; rawData: ScenarioCard` / `"persona"; rawData: PersonaCard`. The existing `switch (card.cardType)` blocks in App.tsx and Library.tsx then narrow automatically and every `as` on those lines deletes. This removes types rather than adding them.

..summary: Four non-character editors re-implement an identical state/save/export host with no shared abstraction

evidence: ScriptEditor.tsx:32-88, ScenarioEditor.tsx:34-88 and PersonaEditor.tsx:35-90 are line-for-line equivalent apart from the card type, the DEFAULT literal, the metadata key passed to `encodeCharaToPng` and the filename suffix: same six useState slots, same `useEffect` syncing outputFileName to `card.name`, same `update`/`clearForNew`/`exportJson`/`exportPng` bodies, and the same `handleSaveToLibrary` including the identical `versionChanged` save-as-new-version rule.
LoreBookEditor.tsx carries the same slots (lines 96-105) and the same `clearForNew`/`exportJson`/`exportPng`/`handleSaveToLibrary` at 164-226, with lorebook-specific extras layered on top.
Because the rule lives in four places, the version-bump behaviour and the 'Unnamed X' fallback have to be kept in sync by hand — a sixth card type means a fifth copy.
detail.suggestion: Extract one hook, e.g. `useCardEditor<T extends { name: string; version: string; tags: string[] }>({ cardType, blank, fileSuffix })` in src/hooks/, returning `{ card, update, imageSrc, setImageSrc, outputFileName, setOutputFileName, saving, status, clearForNew, exportJson, exportPng, saveToLibrary }`. The four editors keep only their JSX and their type-specific fields. This deletes roughly 200 lines net and is the one place in this codebase where a generic genuinely has four concrete instantiations.

..summary: Identical PNG-bytes-to-data-URL helper copy-pasted into two components

evidence: src/components/DecodePNG.tsx:54-58 declares uint8ToDataUrl inside the processFile useCallback: a char-by-char accumulation loop followed by `return "data:image/png;base64," + btoa(bin);`.
src/components/ImportPNG.tsx:37-39 contains the same loop and the same return expression at module scope.
The inverse conversion already lives in a lib module (base64ToBytes in src/lib/carrierImage.ts:33-38), so the codebase's own convention puts this helper in src/lib/.
detail.suggestion: Move it to src/lib/carrierImage.ts as `export function pngBytesToDataUrl(bytes: Uint8Array): string` next to the existing base64ToBytes, and import it in both components. One exported function replaces two inline copies — no new file, no new layer.

..summary: exportPng/handleSaveToLibrary/clearForNew copied verbatim across four editor components

evidence: ScenarioEditor.tsx:66-74, ScriptEditor.tsx:65-74, PersonaEditor.tsx:75-84 and LoreBookEditor.tsx:208-217 contain byte-identical exportPng() bodies apart from the card-type string passed to encodeCharaToPng.

handleSaveToLibrary() is likewise identical at ScenarioEditor.tsx:76-88, ScriptEditor.tsx:76-88, PersonaEditor.tsx:86-98 and LoreBookEditor.tsx:219-232 — same setSaving dance, same `versionChanged` computation, same three-way success ternary, same bare `catch { setMsg("Failed to save to library.", false); }`.

The same four files each repeat clearForNew(), a Partial-patch update(), the same five useState declarations, and an identical `// Auto-sync filename to <type> name` useEffect (LoreBookEditor.tsx:110, PersonaEditor.tsx:46, ScenarioEditor.tsx:45, ScriptEditor.tsx:42).
detail.suggestion: Extract one hook, e.g. `useCardEditorIO(cardType, { card, imageSrc, fileSuffix })` in src/hooks/, returning `{ outputFileName, setOutputFileName, saving, libraryId, exportJson, exportPng, saveToLibrary, clearForNew, status, setMsg }`. Each of the four editors then calls it once and keeps only its own field JSX. This is a net reduction — one implementation replaces four copies and one new file replaces roughly 200 duplicated lines — and it removes the risk that a fix to the save path lands in three editors out of four.

..summary: saveCard and saveAnyCard take incompatible positional parameter lists for the same 'persist a card' job

evidence: saveCard(cardData: TavernCardV2, pngData, imageSrc, platform, existingId?) vs saveAnyCard(cardType, name, rawData, imageSrc, tags, existingId?) — only imageSrc and existingId occupy comparable positions, and saveAnyCard is six positional params.
tags is derived from cardData.data.tags inside saveCard but must be supplied positionally to saveAnyCard; platform is a caller argument in one and hardcoded to cardType in the other.

src/lib/bridge/client.ts defines a private persist(cardType, body, imageSrc, existingId) whose entire body is an if/else picking between the two and shuffling arguments — the adapter exists only because the two signatures disagree.
detail.suggestion: Collapse both into one exported saveLibraryCard(input: { cardType, name?, cardData?, rawData?, pngData?, imageSrc, platform?, tags?, existingId? }): Promise<LibraryCard>, deriving name/tags from cardData when cardType is 'character'. Update the ~6 call sites (bridge/client.ts, CardPreviewPanel, LoreBookEditor, PersonaEditor, ScenarioEditor, ScriptEditor) and delete persist() from bridge/client.ts — this removes a function rather than adding one.

..summary: create_lorebook omits the shared tags field and update_card re-declares `open` without openAfter's data-loss warning

evidence: mcp/src/index.ts defines shared zod shapes `tags` and `openAfter` and uses them in create_character, create_persona, create_scenario, create_script.

create_lorebook's inputSchema has no `tags` entry, so a lorebook created through MCP can never carry tags — even though CardSummary.tags, saveAnyCard's tags parameter, and list_cards all support tags for lorebooks.

update_card declares `open: z.boolean().optional().describe("Bring the card up in the editor afterwards.")` instead of reusing openAfter, dropping the sentence 'opening a card replaces whatever the user is currently editing, and any unsaved work in that panel is lost' — the one tool most likely to be called mid-edit is the one that no longer warns.
create_character uses `character_version` while the other four create_* tools use `version`; this one is defensible (Tavern v2 spec) but is undocumented as deliberate.
detail.suggestion: Add `tags,` to create_lorebook's inputSchema and pass it through to create(); replace update_card's inline `open` declaration with the shared `openAfter` constant. Both are one-line edits in mcp/src/index.ts.

..summary: SortOptions.signal is ignored on the WebLLM backend and onProgress is ignored on the endpoint backend

evidence: SortOptions declares { settings?, target?, onProgress?, signal? } as one public options bag on sortPersonaWithAi and sortPersonaAuto.
sortPersonaWithAi routes opts.signal only into runEndpoint(input, settings, target, opts.signal) and opts.onProgress only into runWebLlm(input, settings, target, opts.onProgress).

settings.backend defaults to 'webllm' (src/lib/personaLlm/settings.ts DEFAULTS), so a caller passing an AbortSignal on the default path gets no cancellation and no error — the model download and inference run to completion.
No caller in src/ passes signal at all today (only SmartImportPanel.tsx calls these functions, via runSort), so the option is advertised and untested.
detail.suggestion: Either honour signal on the WebLLM path (check signal.aborted before getEngine and after the completion resolves, throwing a DOMException 'AbortError'), or split the two backends' capabilities in the type — e.g. document on SortOptions that `signal` applies to the endpoint backend only and `onProgress` to the WebLLM backend only, with a one-line JSDoc on each field. The doc-only fix is the smaller change if cancellation is not actually needed.

..summary: Authenticated bridge peer can delete/overwrite any card with no confirmation and no audit record, unlike every UI path

evidence: src/lib/bridge/client.ts handle() dispatches cards.delete and cards.update straight to deleteCard/persist; the only trace left is setState({ served, lastMethod }) held in memory for the status light.

Every UI destructive path gates on ConfirmModal first — Library.tsx confirmDelete ('Deletes are irreversible and there is no undo, so both paths confirm first'), Templates.tsx, App.tsx clear-card — so the same invariant is enforced for the human and skipped for the agent.
The only mitigation on the agent path is prose in the tool description in mcp/src/index.ts ('There is no undo — confirm with the user first'), which the model may ignore.
detail.suggestion: Give the bridge the same confirmation the UI enforces for the same operations: route cards.delete (and cards.update when it overwrites an existing card) through the existing ConfirmModal via a host hook, so the promise resolves only after the user approves, and append a bounded in-app log of served methods with card id and timestamp instead of only a counter. Reuse ConfirmModal and the registerBridgeHost callback that already exists rather than adding a new permission layer.

..summary: bridge bodyOf() declares Record<string, string> for a body containing arrays and objects

evidence: src/lib/bridge/client.ts:291 `if (c.cardType === "character") return c.cardData?.data as unknown as Record<string, string>;` — TavernCardV2Data has `tags: string[]`, `alternate_greetings: string[]` and `extensions: Record<string, unknown>`.
The lie propagates: updateCard spreads the result into `merged` and then casts it back with `as Record<string, unknown>` before handing it to persist().
detail.suggestion: Declare bodyOf as `Record<string, unknown> | undefined` and read the one string field summarise needs with a local narrowing (`typeof body?.character_version === "string" ? … : undefined`). That drops the double cast in updateCard as well.
